idea: Why most AI agents are built backwards

allowed_claims: Agents and functions have zero access by default and need explicit grants.
A Lemma pod packages data, documents, automation, AI agents, and UI inside one permission boundary.
One pod can replace a scattered stack of point tools for a focused operating loop.
proof_points: The Content Pod is being built directory-first with seeded records and phase-by-phase verification.
LEDflex support workflow is a real pod-style deployment pattern.
Coach Carter shows Telegram capture, structured tables, functions, and a desk working together.
audience_signals: They are skeptical of generic AI writing tools.
They care about real workflow ownership, not demos.
They respond to strong product beliefs backed by shipped proof.

perspectives.label: Contrarian take
perspectives.description: Most agents are designed as chat first, but real work starts with resources and permissions.
perspectives.why_it_fits: The idea already challenges the default way teams think about agents.

perspectives.label: Practical lesson
perspectives.description: What building pods taught us about why agents need state before personality.
perspectives.why_it_fits: It connects the idea to concrete operating architecture.

perspectives.label: Pain post
perspectives.description: Teams do not need another chat box; they need an operating loop that does not leak context.
perspectives.why_it_fits: It starts with a pain content owners and operators already recognize.

perspectives.label: Bold claim
perspectives.description: The operating loop matters more than the interface around it.
perspectives.why_it_fits: It gives the content owner a memorable thesis to test in short-form content.
